title: DPE Record 1.0
description: One Data Protection Exposure record: one named pattern, observed at one target, at one point in time, with retained evidence. A record describes measured behaviour. It is not a finding of unlawfulness; that is for a supervisory authority or a court.

id.description: Permanent identifier. Never reused, never deleted. A withdrawn record keeps its id and its URL.

pattern.description: Slug of the named pattern in the registry, e.g. 'frontrun'. The name is the citable unit; this id is administrative.

kind.description: 'vendor-product' means the exposure sits in the product itself, in its default or documented configuration, and every deployment inherits it.

package.description: Android package name, iOS bundle id, or firmware model.

operator.description: Organisation responsible for the deployment, as named in its own privacy statement.

tlp.description: Traffic Light Protocol 2.0. Governs whether this record may be published. Records at evidence level S are capped at AMBER.

status.description: draft: machine-generated, not reviewed. disclosure: party notified, publication deadline running. disputed: party contests it, contest documented. corrected: substantive content changed after publication. resolved: re-check shows the exposure is gone. withdrawn: the record was wrong; it stays online with this status.

vector.description: See dpe-vector-1.0.md. Describes what was measured, carries no severity.

severity.description: Derived from the vector by a published, versioned rule. Never entered by hand.

credit.description: Who did the work. Permanent and citable, because attribution is what a contributor gets in return. One entry per person or organisation per role; the same person may appear in several roles across records. A contributor may be credited as 'anonymous' and still hold the role: the registry, not the reporter, carries the publication.

name.description: As the contributor wants to be cited, or 'anonymous'.

role.description: measured: ran the capture. reproduced: independently replayed someone else's record, which is what raises detection quality. reported: brought it to the registry without measuring. reviewed: editorial check before publication. disputed: contested it, including from the named party's own side. corrected: fixed an error in a published record.

url.description: Where the contributor wants to be linked, if anywhere.

detection.description: How the exposure was confirmed. Modelled on the Quality of Detection concept from vulnerability scanning: the number describes the method, not the seriousness. It exists so a weak detection method can never be quoted as if it were a strong one.

rule.description: Slug of the detection rule in rules/.

qod.description: static-source 60, network-observed 90, network-with-identifier 95, document-comparison 97 (measurement checked against the party's own published statement), differential 97, third-party-confirmed 99, archival-continuous 99 (for duration, not for current behaviour).

indicator.description: The concrete thing that settled it: a property id, a container id, an endpoint, or the set comparison that was performed.

samples.description: A single capture is a sample, not a scan: behaviour varies with time, location and A/B testing. A record that reproduced 3 of 3 times is a different claim from one that reproduced 1 of 3, and the record must be able to say which.

vantage_points.description: Where each capture egressed. Consent flows are frequently geo-targeted.

basis.description: What carries the finding. 'traffic-property' (a third party received a persistent identifier) is preferred over 'host-list' (the host appears on our list), because the first is a property of the traffic and the second is a classification we made and therefore a thing to argue about. 'own-documents' compares the measurement against the party's own privacy statement or code of conduct, which is the least contestable basis available.

reach.description: How many people the deployment plausibly touches. Reported separately from severity: national reach makes an exposure more important, not more serious.

basis.description: Where the figure comes from, with a source.

assessments.description: Weightings by named parties. Multiple assessments may disagree; each keeps its author. This is where opinion lives, explicitly labelled.

destinations.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 codes of observed destinations, with how each was established. Kept out of the vector so an edge-node change does not alter the vector.

method.description: GeoIP database version is recorded in reproduction.environment.

sources.description: One block per source, each with its own text, date and artefact. Provenance is never merged into a single description.

artefact.description: URL or path of the raw evidence.

reproduction.description: A third party must be able to replay this without the registry's own tooling. The core advantage over CVE, and the reason a record survives contest.

methods.description: At least one method must have tier 'manual' or 'script', so that reproduction never depends on tooling only the registry possesses.

tier.description: manual: browser devtools by hand, no install. script: standalone snippet, one dependency at most. suite: the registry's own scanner, for scale.

commit.description: Pinned commit. The published link is a permalink at this commit, so the cited snippet can never change under the record.

runner.description: A hosted environment where the snippet can be executed without local install.

exit_country.description: Where the hosted runner egresses. Decisive: consent flows and CMP geo-targeting differ per region, so a US-hosted runner may not reproduce an EU observation.

profile.description: A warm profile can carry prior consent and invalidates a CS:PRE claim.

evidence_viewer.description: Where a reader can inspect the retained artefact without installing anything.

independent_confirmation.description: Measurements by third parties with their own permanent result URL. The strongest evidence a record can carry, because the measuring party is not the registry. Also tamper-evident: a party that cleans up after publication cannot alter last week's public scan.

url.description: Permanent result URL held by the third party.

operator.description: Who ran it. An entry run by someone other than the registry carries more weight and should say so.

reproduced_by.description: Independent replays of the snippet itself by a named party.

continuity.description: Archival evidence of how long the exposure has existed. The registry's second advantage over CVE: an uninterrupted run of public snapshots cannot be repaired retroactively, so it turns an incident into a structural finding.

continuous_since.description: Start of the strictly uninterrupted run (ISO date or year-month).

snapshots_consecutive.description: Number of consecutive snapshots carrying the marker. Reported as a lower bound.

earlier_traces.description: Older, non-contiguous traces, reported separately so the headline figure stays strictly defensible.

marker.description: What was searched for in the snapshots, e.g. a property id or container id.

falsifier.description: What would refute this record, and whether it was tested. Mandatory: a record without a tested falsifier cannot leave draft.

evidence.description: Where in the artefact this was checked.

attribution.description: How the flow was attributed to this target. Referer headers are not accepted: stealth instrumentation spoofs them.

products.description: The product layer. A CMP, SDK or tag manager configuration that causes the exposure in its default state is one record with many affected deployments.

configuration.description: Whether the exposure follows from the default configuration or from this deployment's own settings. Decisive for who is responsible.

legal_context.description: The provisions in play and prior decisions on the same pattern. Deliberately named 'context': the record does not assert a breach.

provisions.description: The provisions in play, each tied to a jurisdiction. This is the layer that makes a pattern usable outside one country: the behaviour is the same everywhere in the EEA, only the citation differs. A contributor in another country reuses the pattern, the rule and the reproduction script, and attaches their own national provision.

jurisdiction.description: EU for union-wide instruments, otherwise an ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code.

implements.description: The EU instrument this national provision implements, so equivalents across countries can be lined up.

disclosure.description: Coordinated disclosure trail. Required before status may become 'published'.

response_text.description: The party's own words, quoted, not summarised.

rechecks.description: A record is a moment in time. Re-checks turn an incident into a time series, which is what makes a structural claim possible.

changes.description: Append-only audit trail, machine-generated at field level. Entries are never edited or removed. This is what makes a silent correction impossible.

actor.description: Who or what made the change: a pipeline stage or a named editor.

then.description: A suspicion is never published. Evidence level S caps the record at AMBER.
